teaser: A conductor publishes one append lane per agent, each token sealed to that agent's key: a private channel built from public material.
core_idea: The Web Summit team's conductor runs an inbox vault with one append lane per agent, 34 on the first night. Each lane's write token is published, sealed to that agent's own public key and signed by the conductor, so only that agent can open it and it can verify the issuer. Messages are sealed to the conductor's key, the lane holds only ciphertext, and the drain names the lane. Its first use was agents sending vault keys so they outlive sessions without touching a repository or chat. It needs no shared secret, scales with one run, and could connect teams and companies.

quotes.text: Everything in that file is public, on purpose.
A vault key sent this way never touches the repository, a chat, or a page.
This pattern does something that usually needs infrastructure, with almost none.
